newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Kuwait opens term naphtha talks with Asian buyers.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait opens term naphtha talks with Asian buyers.

text.p: Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) opened term-contract naphtha supply talks in Singapore on Monday with about a dozen Asian buyers, industry sources said.
They said KPC was initially seeking an idea on buyers' bid levels for supplies between March 1997 to February 1998.
"They just want to hear bids and are not saying anything," one trader said of the talks Monday.

Traders said they expected bids to be firmer than the last round at $7.90 per tonne over MidEast quotes, which covered August 1996 to July 1997 cargoes, and even the latest conclusion by a MidEast refinery at around $11.00.
Bids "will go from $12 to $15," one trader said.
Naphtha supplies are expected to show a deficit in supplies for the next few years.
Researchers at Hawaii's East-West Center forecast a net deficit in supplies in 1997 of 488,000 barrels-per-day (bpd), falling to 441,000 bpd in 1998.
